pins.definition: Making little or no noise, or having no noise.
Making very little noise; low in volume.
Low in intensity, strength, or volume; barely noticeable.

situation: A librarian in a large, silent library holds a finger to her lips while looking at a student who has just dropped a heavy book.
subject: the absence of sound
brief: In a vast library with tall shelves, a librarian stands with a single finger pressed to her lips in a gesture of silence. A student stands frozen, looking down at a thick book that has just fallen to the floor, while the surrounding air is depicted with soft, motionless watercolor textures to emphasize the stillness of the room.
prompt: In a vast library with tall shelves, a librarian stands with a single finger pressed to her lips in a gesture of silence. A student stands frozen, looking down at a thick book that has just fallen to the floor, while the surrounding air is depicted with soft, motionless watercolor textures to emphasize the stillness of the room. loose watercolour washes over confident ink linework, blooms and granulation in the pigment, warm paper grain, the warmth of a picture book for adults. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
